mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of quarters where GDPC1 falls by 2% or more.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) that falls below 5% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE drops below 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of 1% or more over three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing output and reduced corporate earnings potential, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by 1% or more for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero in periods where INDPRO declines by 1% or more for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in FEDFUNDS and a fall in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) of more than 0.5% month-over-month indicates aggressive monetary tightening coinciding with cooling inflation, which historically has been associated with delayed but ultimately negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as growth concerns dominate.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases AND CPIAUCSL drops > 0.5% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of episodes where FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls by more than 0.5% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) of 5% or more over two consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises by 5% or more for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in periods where HOUST increases by 5% or more for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) over two months signals a situation where job creation is insufficient to absorb new entrants, indicating structural labor market slack and negative earnings revision risk, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases AND UNRATE increases over two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of episodes where PAYEMS and UNRATE both rise for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of 2% or more over four consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue and profit expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls by 2% or more for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero in periods where RSAFS declines by 2% or more for four consecutive months.
